description: Found by the fz-go4.22 re-enable batch (2026-07-04, at 6912ad3de/d49562986). matrix::tail_recursion::interp is an ACTIVE (non-deferred, non-ignored) test that is FLAKY even single-threaded and in isolation: observed passing 2/2 then failing 2/2 in the same session on BOTH the worktree and the pristine coordinator checkout at d49562986. This is worse than a deterministic red or an ignored test — an active flaky test poisons the fixture_matrix run-to-run (it is one of the ~19 matrix failures but intermittently). Distinct from the deterministic reds (native.rs:3123, enum_take_drop_split codegen, actor_ring). Likely the .28.6 nondeterminism family (schedule-dependent interp result) but must be confirmed: reproduce, capture the two divergent outcomes (is it a wrong-answer flip like repr_seam_enum_count_after_reduce2, or a pass/crash flip?), and trace whether it's the ReturnType-widening / demand-cone-membership variance. If it is .28.6-rooted, fold into that fix; if distinct, own ticket. Meanwhile it should NOT be trusted as a green gate.
title: tail_recursion::interp is flaky (non-deterministic pass/fail) even single-threaded in isolation
